title: RIGS: Mechanized Combat League
subtitle: A pilot in the middle of the arena
summary: RIGS: Mechanized Combat League is Guerrilla Cambridge's virtual-reality arena shooter, released with PlayStation VR on 13 October 2016.
body: RIGS: Mechanized Combat League is Guerrilla Cambridge's virtual-reality arena shooter, released with PlayStation VR on 13 October 2016. Pilots compete in a futuristic professional sport using large armed machines called Rigs. Teams move through arenas inspired by real-world locations, combining combat with the objectives of a match. The headset places the player inside the machine, turning the height of a platform and the approach of another Rig into parts of the sporting space that must be read while fighting.

Matches divide six competitors into two teams of three. Destroying an opposing Rig scores a takedown, while different competition types change the larger objective. Four classes provide the foundation for twenty-four machines, each with a weapon loadout and a particular ability. The selection matters to how a player contributes: a machine's mobility, weapons and special benefit shape the positions it can use effectively. The arena becomes a shared tactical problem, with teammates needing to combine their different machines rather than simply chase the nearest target.

Five-minute matches split into two halves give the contest a clear sporting frame. Barnabas and Arnold composed the music, and Guerrilla's Decima technology supported the production. RIGS joined the original headset's launch lineup as an experiment in competitive virtual-reality action. Its online service closed in August 2022, an important boundary in the history of a game built partly around team competition. The original design remains an example of placing a familiar arena match inside a vehicle whose size and cockpit are experienced through a headset.
